name: Altay Therapeutics
description: Altay Therapeutics is a biopharmaceutical company developing first-in-class small molecule inhibitors of disease-causing transcription factors. Transcription factors have long been considered undruggable, but Altay's proprietary discovery platform identifies novel allosteric binding sites, enabling the design of highly selective inhibitors. The company's lead candidate, DX5057, is the first orally administered small molecule inhibitor of DUX4, the transcription factor that drives facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). FSHD is a progressive and debilitating genetic muscle disease characterized by asymmetric weakness and atrophy of the facial, shoulder, arm and leg muscles, and there are currently no approved treatments. DX5057 has shown strong efficacy in preclinical models of FSHD and has been granted Orphan Drug Designation by the FDA. As an oral therapy, it has the potential to offer patients a more convenient long-term treatment option. The company is based in California, USA.

name: Carisma Therapeutics
description: Carisma Therapeutics is a biotechnology company specializing in the development of innovative immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer. The company focuses on engineering Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) macrophages, a type of immune cell, to enhance their ability to recognize and eliminate cancer cells. Carisma's proprietary technology involves genetically modifying macrophages to express CARs, which are designed to recognize specific tumor antigens. By targeting these antigens, CAR macrophages can effectively locate and destroy cancer cells in a targeted manner. The company's approach harnesses the unique characteristics of macrophages, which are natural immune cells with inherent abilities to engulf and destroy pathogens and abnormal cells. Carisma's CAR macrophages have the potential to overcome limitations associated with other cell-based immunotherapies, such as CAR-T cell therapies. The pipeline is composed of several programs, with the lead program targeting HER-2 expressing tumors.

name: ABRA Auto Body & Glass
description: In 2014, H&F acquired ABRA, a leading multi-state operator (“MSO”) of auto body and glass repair centers. ABRA provided repair solutions that enabled its insurance company partners to improve customer satisfaction and drive policyholder retention while also reducing repair costs in the claims process. In 2019, H&F acquired Caliber Collision and merged it with ABRA.

name: Action
description: In 2020, H&F made a minority investment in Action. Established in 1993, Benelux-based Action is a leading non-food discount retailer in Europe. Large-scale procurement, flexible assortment, optimal distribution, and a cost-conscious corporate culture ensure very low prices.

name: Activant Solutions, Inc.
description: In 2006, H&F acquired Activant Solutions, a leading provider of specialized software, services, and information for distribution businesses and their customers. The Company was comprised of three primary segments: the Hardlines, the Wholesale Distribution segment, and the Autoparts Aftermarket segment. Activant Solutions was sold and combined with Epicor Software Corporation in 2011.

name: Advanstar Communications
description: In 1996, H&F invested in Advanstar, a leading provider of integrated business-to-business marketing communications solutions. Advanstar was sold in 2000.

name: AlixPartners, LLP
description: In 2006, H&F led a recapitalization of AlixPartners, a global consulting and business advisory firm with services ranging from performance improvement, turnaround and restructuring, litigation advisory and information management. AlixPartners was sold in 2012.

name: Allfunds S.A.
description: In 2017, H&F acquired Allfunds, a leading European business-to-business (“B2B”) mutual fund distribution platform. The Company serves as a global marketplace, helping financial institutions gain access to third-party mutual funds and ETFs for their end customers.

name: Applied Systems
description: In 2014, H&F acquired Applied Systems, a leading provider of insurance software, including Broker Management Software and data exchange between agencies, brokerages, carriers, and their clients. The Company’s software automates property and casualty insurance transactions for customers throughout the P&C insurance distribution channel.

name: Arch Capital Group
description: In 2001, H&F co-led a recapitalization of Arch Capital, a publicly traded reinsurance and insurance company based in Bermuda. H&F fully exited its investment in Arch Capital in 2007.

name: Artisan Partners Asset Management Inc.
description: In 2006, H&F invested in Artisan Partners, a global investment management firm providing a broad range of high-value-added investment strategies. Artisan completed its initial public offering in 2013 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2014.

name: Associated Materials Incorporated
description: In 2010, H&F acquired Associated Materials, a vertically integrated manufacturer and distributor of exterior residential building products in North America. Associated Materials distributed its products on a wholesale basis through an extensive dual distribution network located throughout the United States and Canada. Associated Materials was fully exited in 2020.

name: At Home
description: In 2021, H&F acquired At Home, a leading value retailer of home décor products with a broad selection at everyday low prices. At Home’s assortment includes textiles, housewares, garden, wall décor, and furniture, among others, and the majority of its products are unbranded, private label or specifically designed for At Home. The Company’s unique merchandising strategy allows it to rapidly identify trends and engineer products to provide desirable aesthetics at attractive price points. At Home was fully exited in 2025.

name: athenahealth
description: In 2022, H&F acquired athenahealth, a leading provider of cloud-based enterprise software solutions for medical groups in the United States. The Company partners with ambulatory care providers to support the delivery of leading clinical and financial outcomes. athenahealth’s solutions, including electronic health records, revenue cycle management, telehealth, payments and patient engagement tools, enable its customers to increase clinical efficiency, optimize financial performance, improve patient care outcomes, and support providers in accelerating their shift toward value-based care.

name: AutoScout24
description: In 2020, H&F made an investment in AutoScout24, a leading European digital car classifieds business based in Munich, Germany. AutoScout24 connects car dealers and private sellers with consumers looking to buy and finance a used or new car.

name: Axel Springer AG
description: In 2003, H&F partnered with the Springer family to acquire an interest in Axel Springer AG, Germany’s largest publisher of newspapers and second largest publisher of magazines. H&F fully exited its investment in Axel Springer in 2010.

name: Baker Tilly
description: In 2024, H&F made an investment in Baker Tilly, a leading US Advisory CPA firm, performing audit, tax and advisory services, and primarily serving middle market clients. Baker Tilly will operate under an alternative practice structure pursuant to which H&F will not have an equity interest in the audit and attest services business of Baker Tilly.

name: Belron
description: In 2021, H&F made a minority investment in Belron. Founded in South Africa, Belron is a leading global vehicle glass repair & replacement provider. Belron serves customers globally, operating mainly through the Safelite (USA) and Carglass (Central Europe) brands.

name: Blackbaud, Inc.
description: In 1999, H&F acquired Blackbaud, a leading provider of software and related services designed specifically for nonprofit organizations, selling mission-critical fundraising, accounting and school administration software and services. Blackbaud completed its initial public offering in 2004 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2006.

name: Caliber Collision
description: Caliber Collision is a leading multi-site operator (“MSO”) of auto body collision repair centers in the United States with a nationwide footprint. Caliber provides repair solutions that enable its insurance company partners to improve customer satisfaction and drive policyholder retention while also reducing repair costs in the claims process. In 2019, H&F acquired Caliber Collision and merged it with ABRA Auto Body & Glass, LP, an investment made in 2014.

name: CarProof Corporation
description: In 2013, H&F made an investment in CarProof, a leading provider of vehicle history reports (“VHRs”) in Canada. CarProof was founded in 2000 to increase transparency, trust, and efficiency in the purchase of used cars. CarProof was sold to IHS in 2015.

name: Catalina Marketing Corporation
description: In 2007, in a take-private transaction, H&F acquired Catalina, a provider of consumer-driven marketing solutions for the world’s leading CPG retailers and brands. H&F sold a majority stake in 2014 and fully exited its investment in 2019.

name: Change Healthcare
description: In 2008, H&F invested in Change Healthcare (previously called Emdeon), a leading provider of revenue and payment cycle management and clinical information exchange solutions. Change Healthcare’s product and service offerings integrated and automated key business and administrative functions for healthcare payers and providers throughout the patient encounter. Change Healthcare was fully exited in 2020.

name: Checkmarx
description: In 2020, H&F acquired Checkmarx, a market leader in the Application Security Testing market. Founded in 2006 and based in Israel, Checkmarx has a portfolio of products that enable developers and security professionals to identify software vulnerabilities during the development process.

name: Circana
description: Circana is a leading provider of market research on durable consumer goods (e.g., consumer electronics, apparel, home appliances, toys, books), foodservice, and consumer packaged goods. Circana collects online and brick-and-mortar point of sale data from retailers, using this data to deliver essential insights to many of the world’s leading consumer companies. In 2021, H&F acquired The NPD Group, a leading provider of market research, and in 2022, merged NPD with Information Resources, Inc. (“IRI”), renaming the combined company Circana. The combination brings together complementary data assets across a broad range of industries to create a scale global technology, analytics and data provider.

name: Claritev Corporation
description: In 2016, H&F acquired MultiPlan, one of the largest third-party providers of cost-containment solutions to U.S. health plans. In February 2025, MultiPlan rebranded to Claritev. Health insurance companies rely on Claritev as the industry-wide solution for processing and generating savings on claims, primarily those that fall outside insurers’ internal provider networks.

name: Cordis
description: In 2021, H&F acquired Cordis, a leading provider of cardiovascular and endovascular medical devices. Founded in 1966, the Company has a long history of innovation in high-quality and minimally-invasive cardiovascular technology. Its products are primarily used in procedures to diagnose and treat the narrowing or blockage of arteries.

name: Curriculum Associates
description: In 2022, H&F made a minority investment in Curriculum Associates. Curriculum Associates is a leading adaptive learning platform for U.S. K-12 schools and districts. Their flagship product, i-Ready, closely integrates learning diagnostics with content, enabling educators to deliver highly tailored instruction to address the diverse needs of students in a classroom. With a broad suite of supplemental, core basal, and formative assessment products, Curriculum Associates has become a well-respected K-12 education company in the North America.

name: Digitas, Inc.
description: In 1999, H&F made an investment in Digitas, a leading global marketing services organization. Digitas completed its initial public offering in 2000 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2004.

name: DoubleClick, Inc.
description: In 2005, in a take-private transaction, H&F acquired DoubleClick, a leading provider of technology and data solutions for advertising agencies, web publishers, marketers, and catalogers to help plan, execute and analyze their marketing programs. DoubleClick was sold to Google in 2008.

name: Edelman Financial Engines
description: Edelman Financial Engines is one of the largest independent investment advisors in America, with a nationwide network of advisors. The company provides holistic, personalized financial planning and advice, offering this service through automated technology-enabled solutions and in-person advice via a financial planner. In 2018, H&F took private Financial Engines and merged it with Edelman Financial, an investment made in 2015.

name: Eller Media Company, Inc.
description: In 1995, H&F partnered with Karl Eller to acquire Eller Media (formerly known as Patrick Media), one of the largest outdoor advertising companies in the U.S. The Company was sold to Clear Channel Communications in 1997.

name: Ellucian, Inc.
description: Ellucian, a leading global provider of software products and services to higher education institutions, was created in 2012 when H&F acquired SunGard’s higher education division and combined it with Datatel, a 2009 investment. Ellucian was sold in 2015.

name: Enverus
description: In 2021, H&F acquired Enverus, a leading provider of U.S. energy data analytics and software. The Company’s products are used by engineers, executives, investors, and accountants to manage a variety of mission critical workflows in the energy world, including asset valuation, asset development, energy production, ESG compliance, strategic sourcing, and back-office automation.

name: Formula One Holdings Limited
description: In 2000, H&F invested in Formula One, the holding company responsible for the commercial development and administration of the FIA Formula One Grand Prix Championship as well as annual Grand Prix races. In the same year, the Company was sold to EM.TV & Merchandising AG.

name: Franklin Resources, Inc.
description: In 1992, H&F invested in Franklin Resources, one of the then largest mutual fund managers globally, to facilitate its acquisition of Templeton, Galbraith & Hansberger, Ltd. H&F completed the sale of its investment in Franklin Resources in 1997.

name: Gartmore Investment Management Limited
description: In 2006, H&F acquired Gartmore, a London-based leading independent, multi-product asset management firm providing traditional and alternative investment products to retail and institutional investors, from Nationwide Mutual Insurance Company. Gartmore completed its initial public offering on the London Stock Exchange in 2009 and was subsequently acquired by the Henderson Group plc in 2011.

name: Gaztransport & Technigaz S.A.S.
description: In 2008, H&F invested in Gaztransport & Techigaz (“GTT”), a highly-specialized French marine technology company that designed membrane containment systems for the maritime transportation and storage of liquefied natural gas. GTT completed its initial public offering on the Paris Euronext in 2014 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2015.

name: Genesys
description: In 2016, H&F made an investment in Genesys, a leading provider of customer engagement software to large enterprises around the globe. The Company empowers its customers to create effortless omni-channel customer experiences, journeys, and relationships.

name: GeoVera Insurance Group Holdings, Ltd.
description: In 2005, H&F co-led the acquisition of GeoVera, a specialty property and casualty insurer and reinsurer providing coverage for clients with significant catastrophe exposures, from St. Paul Travelers. H&F completed the sale of its investment in 2012.

name: Getty Images, Inc.
description: In 2008, in a take-private transaction, H&F acquired Getty Images, a leading creator, aggregator and distributor of visual and multimedia content to creative and communication professionals. Getty Images offered one of the world’s largest marketplaces for distributing, searching, licensing, and managing digital imagery and multimedia. The Company was sold in 2012.

name: Global Music Rights
description: In 2024, H&F invested in Global Music Rights, a Performing Rights Organization (“PRO”) serving top-tier songwriters. As a PRO, GMR collects fees on behalf of songwriters, composers, and music publishers when their music is used by licensees. GMR’s licensees include digital streaming providers, streaming and linear TV providers, satellite and terrestrial radio stations, and live music venues, among others. The Company was founded in 2013 and is headquartered in Los Angeles.

name: Goodman Global, Inc.
description: In 2008, in a take-private transaction, H&F acquired Goodman Global, a leading domestic unit manufacturer and distributor of heating, ventilation and air conditioning products for residential and light commercial use. Goodman Global was sold to Daikin Industries, Ltd in 2012.

name: Grocery Outlet, Inc.
description: In 2014, H&F acquired Grocery Outlet, a leading extreme-value retailer with locations across the West Coast and Pennsylvania. Grocery Outlet’s highly differentiated sourcing model – purchasing excess inventory from trusted CPG partners – enabled the company to offer its customers significant savings in a fun, treasure hunt shopping environment. Grocery Outlet completed its initial public offering on the Nasdaq in 2019 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2020.

name: Grosvenor Capital Management
description: In 2007, H&F invested in Grosvenor, one of the world’s largest and most diversified independent alternative asset management firms. The Company offered comprehensive public and private markets solutions and a broad suite of investment and advisory choices that spanned hedge funds, private equity, and various credit and specialty strategies. Grosvenor GCM was fully exited in 2020.

name: HUB International Limited
description: In 2013, H&F acquired HUB International, a leading global insurance brokerage providing property and casualty, life and health, employee benefits, investment and risk management products and services through offices located in the United States and Canada. The Company is structured around regional hubs, which give its brokers and consultants the flexibility to address local market needs while leveraging the economies of scale, technology, and operating efficiencies associated with a multinational brokerage.

name: Intergraph Corporation
description: In 2006, H&F co-led the acquisition of Intergraph, a leading provider of spatial information management software and services used by security organizations, businesses, and governments to turn vast amounts of complex data into visual representations, allowing for faster, more effective operational decisions. Intergraph was sold to Hexagon AB in 2010.

name: Internet Brands, Inc.
description: In 2010, H&F acquired Internet Brands, a vertically focused online solutions company serving the automotive, health, legal, home and travel verticals. The Company’s portfolio of assets included consumer websites as well as end-to-end web presence offerings. Internet Brands was sold in 2014.

name: IRIS Software Group Limited
description: In 2007, H&F acquired two of the UK’s leading vertical application software and services companies and combined them to form IRIS, a leading provider of industry-specific software solutions to accountancy practices, law firms and not-for-profit organizations. The Company was sold in 2011.

name: LPL Financial Holdings, Inc.
description: In 2005, H&F co-led the acquisition of LPL, the then largest independent brokerage firm in the United States. LPL completed its initial public offering in 2010 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2013.

name: Medline
description: In 2021, H&F acquired Medline, a vertically integrated manufacturer and distributor of medical surgical products to hospitals, post-acute facilities and physician offices. Medline’s global manufacturing, sourcing and distribution network enables it to partner with healthcare providers globally, delivering products and solutions that reduce costs, increase supply chain efficiency and improve overall quality of care.

name: Mehiläinen
description: In 2025, H&F made an investment in Mehiläinen, a leading healthcare and social care provider in Finland with a fast-growing international presence. Mehiläinen operates with a technology-enabled model and an inhouse developed digital platform that drives superior patient experience and employee productivity.

name: Mitchell International Holdings, Inc.
description: In 2000, H&F acquired Mitchell, a leading provider of data, software, auto casualty and enterprise claims solutions to the automobile insurance and collision repair industries. Mitchell was sold in 2007.

name: Mondrian Investment Partners Ltd.
description: In 2004, H&F invested alongside management to buy control of Mondrian (formerly, Delaware International Advisors Limited), a London-based value-oriented equity and fixed income money manager, primarily for U.S. institutional clients. H&F completed the sale of its investment in Mondrian in 2011.

name: Nasdaq Stock Market LLC
description: In 2001, H&F invested in The Nasdaq Stock Market, one of the world’s leading stock markets. In 2005, H&F supported Nasdaq’s acquisition of INET (the electronic communication network of Instinet) through a follow-on investment. H&F completed the sale of its investment in Nasdaq in 2007.

name: Nets A/S
description: In 2018, H&F led a take-private transaction of Nets, a leading payments processing utility for the Nordics region. Nets connected banks, businesses, public sector organizations, merchants and consumers through an international network facilitating digital payments. In 2021, H&F completed a merger between Nets and Nexi.

name: Nexi
description: In 2021, H&F completed a merger between Nets, an investment made in 2018 and a leading merchant acquirer and issuing processor in the Nordics, DACH and Poland, and Nexi, a leading payments company providing Merchant Acquiring, Issuer Processing and Digital Payments solutions to a wide range of Italian banks, merchants and consumers. Together, the combined company is one of the largest European payments technology providers connecting banks, businesses, public sector organizations, merchants and consumers through an international network facilitating digital payments.

name: Nielsen N.V.
description: In 2006, H&F was part of an investor group that acquired The Nielsen Company, a leading global information and measurement company providing clients with an understanding of consumers and their behavior. Nielsen completed its initial public offering in 2011 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2015.

name: Ode with Anthropic
description: In 2026, H&F made an investment in Ode with Anthropic, a newly formed company focused on AI transformation services, purpose-built to accelerate enterprise AI deployment at scale. Ode with Anthropic brings together senior Anthropic Applied AI leadership and world-class forward deployed engineering talent to deliver high-impact AI transformation programs to enterprises.

name: OpenLink International Holdings, Inc.
description: In 2011, H&F acquired OpenLink, a leading provider of cross-asset trading and risk management software and services, with particular strength in energy and commodity trading and risk management solutions for energy companies and financial institutions. The Company’s products helped clients manage their front-to-back energy, commodity, and financial instrument trading functions. OpenLink was sold in 2019.

name: PARIS RE Holdings Limited
description: In 2006, H&F was the largest shareholder among an investor group that acquired PARIS RE, a global multi-line property & casualty reinsurer, from its parent AXA Group. In 2007, PARIS RE completed its initial public offering on the Paris Euronext and in 2009, was acquired by PartnerRe, a publicly-traded global multi-line reinsurer. H&F fully exited its investment in 2014.

name: Pharmaceutical Product Development, LLC
description: In 2011, H&F co-led a take-private transaction of PPD, a leading global contract research organization providing drug discovery, development, lifecycle management and laboratory services. PPD applied innovative technologies, therapeutic expertise and a commitment to quality to help clients and partners accelerate the delivery of safe and effective therapeutics and maximize the returns on their R&D investments. PPD was sold to Thermo Fisher in 2021.

name: PointClickCare
description: In 2020, H&F made an investment in PointClickCare, a leading provider of cloud-based software solutions for the long-term and post-acute care industries. The Company’s software-as-a-service platform provides the core clinical and administrative system of record and a comprehensive suite of workflow management tools for Skilled Nursing, Senior Living and Home Health providers.

name: ProSiebenSat.1 Media AG
description: In 2003, H&F was part of an investor group that acquired control of ProSiebenSat.1, Germany’s then largest television broadcasting company with four German TV channels. H&F’s investment in ProSiebenSat.1 was sold in 2007.

name: Renaissance Learning, Inc.
description: In 2014, H&F acquired Renaissance Learning, a leading provider of cloud-based assessment, teaching, and learning solutions for K-12 schools and districts. The Company’s software offered proprietary reading quizzes, formative student assessments, and math practice materials. Renaissance was sold in 2018.

name: Safe-Guard
description: In 2024, H&F acquired Safe-Guard, a leading provider of auto warranty products in the U.S. and Canada. The company primarily works with automotive original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and auto dealers to design and administer protection products sold at auto dealerships.

name: Scout24 Holding GmbH
description: In 2014, H&F acquired Scout24, a leading European internet company, from its parent Deutsche Telekom. Scout24 operated several classifieds websites in Germany and Western Europe, providing contact leads and additional value-added technology and solutions to real estate agents and auto dealers, as well as directly to consumers. Scout24 completed its initial public offering on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2015 and H&F fully exited its investment in 2018.

name: Sedgwick CMS
description: In 2010, H&F co-led the acquisition of Sedgwick, a leading provider of innovative claims and productivity management solutions delivering cost-effective claims administration, medical management, risk consulting and related services to clients in the U.S. and Canada. H&F completed the sale of its investment in 2014.

name: Sheridan Holdings, Inc.
description: In 2007, H&F acquired Sheridan Healthcare, a leading provider of physician services to hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and other healthcare facilities, primarily in the areas of anesthesiology, neonatology, emergency medicine and radiology. Sheridan Healthcare was sold to AmSurg Corporation in 2014.

name: SimpliSafe
description: In 2018, H&F acquired SimpliSafe, a leading provider of residential monitored security solutions. The company’s proprietary security systems are sold to consumers on a “DIY” installation basis, offering customers a full range of features including intrusion and fire detection, video and smart home integration.

name: Snap One
description: In 2017, H&F acquired Snap One, a leading eCommerce provider in the connected home sector. The Company sells proprietary-branded audio/video (“AV”), security, networking, and automation products to residential and commercial AV dealers. name: Palveera
description: Palveera is a brand of LEON Mobility GmbH and emerged from the operations of XOO, the charging infrastructure with integrated advertising. Palveera is developing an edge AI platform that enables real-time interpretation of physical environments and makes the information gathered available via a shared event and context layer—either through an API to existing operational, security, and analytics systems or through its own applications. The platform operates in two stages. At the deployment site, edge AI models process multimodal signals from cameras, microphones, and environmental and IoT sensors, translating them into anonymous, structured events. Continuous video and audio data never leave the site. On-site responses occur locally and without an internet connection. In the backend, events from all sites are linked across sensors, locations, and time to form context relevant to decision-making. This reveals recurring, previously unidentified patterns. After validation, these patterns give rise to new missions that are rolled out as software to the existing network without having to build a new sensor and data stack for each use case. The platform is vendor-neutral and integrates both existing and proprietary sensor technology. Palveera pursues a dual-use approach. In the civilian sector, the platform enables applications for operational optimization, environmental and traffic analyses, digital outdoor advertising, and the monitoring of technical facilities. In the security sector, the same technological foundation supports the detection of theft, break-ins, sabotage, drones, and other anomalies at technical facilities, critical infrastructure, and in public spaces. The distributed architecture is designed to generate cross-location situational awareness for moving objects such as drones—information that a single sensor cannot provide.

Based on a patented technology, these eyeglasses offer presbyopes clear vision at all distances without levelling down aesthetic standards. Presbyopia appears by age 40-45 with increasing difficulties to focus at near distances and affects 400 million people in Europe, Japan and North America. Progressive lenses, featuring a vertical gradient of optical power, are today the best compromise to presbyopia correction. Still about 10% of presbyopes are very unsatisfied with these lenses, experiencing a reduced quality of life. Laclarée’s product has been designed to answer this demand, corresponding to about 2 b€/y. Our solution relies on a disruptive fluid-filled doublet-lens activated by low-power microfluidic actuators inserted in the eyeglass arms and driven by a miniature infrared distance sensor. The lens offers a large field of view, is as transparent as any other ophthalmic lens and is compatible with most lens shapes and frame styles. Laclarée’s team is highly motivated and gathers extensive skills in optics, microfluidic and vision science. The founder of Laclarée is an experienced entrepreneur, he has successfully established a world-leading company in variable optics for cameras. The team has achieved the Proof of Concept, with a fully functional portable demonstrator, enabling a small scale trial with presbyopic people and raising a marked interest in the ecosystem. Laclarée just closed its first seed investor round with Kreaxi and High-Tech Gründerfonds (HTGF).

name: Wise
description: When we send money from one account to another, exchanging currencies along the way, we usually get shortchanged. The most notorious method for transferring money internationally is the airport currency counter, but doing it through the bank is nearly as expensive, with exorbitant exchange rates and other fees costing consumers as much as 5% of the transaction value. The worst part is that patrons are left in the dark about how much they’re losing because fees are often hidden in the exchange rates. Wise (formerly TransferWise) offers a much better alternative. The fast-growing online service uses only real exchange rates (the ones you see on Google) and offers low, transparent fees—often 80% to 90% less than traditional banks. Wise has created an entirely new infrastructure for sending payments globally, building direct connections between banks so that transfers are both cheaper and faster. The fintech company’s product is also evolving rapidly, with services for businesses and multi-currency borderless accounts for frequent travelers. Since launching in 2011, Wise has been revolutionizing the way we send and receive money internationally, creating a system perfectly suited to the interconnected world of today.

description: At Congruent, we build radars for end-to-end autonomous systems. The most advanced autonomous systems are trained as a single neural network from raw sensor data to navigation actions. For a sensor to be included in these pipelines sensor stacks requires two key properties: access to raw sensor data and a high-fidelity sensor simulator. Current automotive radars have neither, they output heavily processed point clouds and no raw radar simulator exists for driving scenes. Congruent solves both problems: a radar architecture that exposes raw data, paired with a world model based radar simulator. Radar is the only depth sensor at a price point that scales to every car on the road and works in all weather conditions. Congruent is building the radar compatible with the training architectures that will make mass-market vehicles autonomous.

name: Kerys Software
description: KERYS Software is a Deeptech software publisher whose goal is to help companies reduce their infrastructure costs, exposure to cyber-threats and carbon footprint by rethinking how their employees are equipped. KERYS Software offers a unique solution that allows multiple work environments to be pooled on a single computer in a completely secure manner, without compromising performance. Users and administrators can switch from one operating system to another with a single click, on a single workstation. Kerys Software' innovative microkernel ensures high security through strict isolation between environments, while avoiding the usual overload of virtualisation. KERYS Software's solution can therefore run multiple virtual machines on a single physical host with near-bare-metal performance and robust security, compliant with DORA and NIS2 standards. KERYS Software customers benefit from significant and immediate savings thanks to the reduction of IT equipment used by employees, as well as improved productivity thanks to an easy switch between environments. As a mission-driven company, KERYS Software brings a substantial reduction in corporate carbon footprint by reducing the amount of IT equipment purchased and used, perfectly aligning with stringent ESG policies.

name: Genentech
description: Genentech isn't just a Kleiner Perkins investment; it's part of our DNA. Genentech was co-founded in 1976 by a young KP partner who had been closely tracking breakthrough research in recombinant DNA technology. Over a beer, the partnership was struck: Kleiner Perkins would provide seed capital, and together they would build an entirely new kind of company. KP didn't just write a check. KP partners joined the board and helped the company pioneer a new way to attract scientific talent, pulling researchers out of academia and into industry for the first time. When Roche acquired full control of the company in 2009, Genentech was valued at $100 billion.

name: Google
description: In 1999, Andy Bechtolsheim introduced us to two Stanford graduates, Larry Page and Sergey Brin. They'd built PageRank, a superior search algorithm that overwhelmed Stanford's network with demand. Banished from campus, they needed capital and scale—fast. Their 17-page deck had just two pages of numbers and three cartoons. As the eighteenth search engine with no business model and no team, they faced long odds. But when John Doerr asked how big Google would be, they answered: "$10 billion in revenue." We wrote our largest check ever. The founders weren't sold on traditional management or recruiting a CEO. John connected them with Scott Cook, Bill Gates, Andy Grove, and Steve Jobs for advice. The executive search led to Eric Schmidt, an experienced tech leader from Sun Microsystems. We helped build their team with Wayne Rosing (VP Engineering) and Jonathan Rosenberg (SVP Product), introduced OKRs for goal-setting, and brought in executive coach Bill Campbell to develop leadership skills. Our investment in Google delivered exceptional returns and transformed how the world accesses information. John continues as a board director of Alphabet, Inc.

name: Intuit
description: When Intuit was founded in 1983, popular understanding of how personal computers could be used was confined to basic word processing and spreadsheets. The founder saw something different: a chance to bring personal finance software to everyday households. Kleiner Perkins backed the company in 1990, and from the start the partnership was an active one. When Microsoft launched a direct competitor to Quicken, KP helped Intuit fight back and win. When it was time to find a new CEO, KP helped develop the candidate list, ultimately landing on a legendary Silicon Valley executive who took the helm in 1994. When Microsoft came back with an acquisition offer, KP was at the table for those negotiations too. The Department of Justice ultimately blocked the deal, and Intuit proceeded as an independent company and went from success to success. Today it is one of the most enduring software businesses ever built, a testament to what happens when a simple insight about everyday life meets the right backing at the right moment.

name: Netscape
description: Before Netscape, the internet existed but most people had no way in. Kleiner Perkins backed Netscape in 1994, betting that a fast, graphical browser could unlock the web for everyday users and spark a new era of commerce and communication. John Doerr joined the board, and in late 1994 the company shipped Netscape Navigator, one of the first browsers that made it genuinely easy to access and navigate the internet. The company's 1995 IPO priced at a $2.9 billion valuation, becoming one of the defining moments of the dot-com era. Netscape marked the beginning of the Internet Age, and while the company no longer exists, its legacy lives on in Mozilla, the open-source project built from Netscape's code. The investment also marked something else: proof that KP could identify not just great companies, but entirely new epochs.

name: Sun Microsystems
description: In the early 1980s, existing computing technology operated in proprietary, walled gardens. A KP partner joined the board and later took a sabbatical from the firm to work directly with Sun, helping develop the SPARC microprocessor. Sun's growth was explosive, expanding its range of products to include Java, the Solaris operating system, and SPARC, and contributing significantly to Unix, RISC processors, thin client computing, and virtualized computing. The relationship ran deep in both directions: Sun became something of a farm system for Silicon Valley, and several of its founders and leaders went on to become partners at Kleiner Perkins.

description: Upheat is a Finnish cleantech company founded by Timo Pulkki, Juha Saari, Juha Lammi, Toni Pennanen and Olli Kuismanen, building the next generation of high-temperature heat pumps for industrial process heat. Its oil-free technology recovers waste heat and upgrades it into valuable 100–200°C heat and steam, helping industrial companies reduce both energy costs and fossil fuel use. Upheat’s heat pumps are designed for energy-intensive industries where high temperatures have traditionally made electrification difficult. By integrating directly into existing systems, they enable manufacturers across food and beverage, pulp, paper and wood, pharmaceuticals and chemicals to reuse energy that would otherwise be lost – reducing primary energy consumption by up to 80%.

The company’s proprietary laser-based tracking technology is designed to detect and monitor objects in Low Earth Orbit with a level of precision and coverage beyond what is currently available from commercial systems.

Sono’s platform handles high-volume customer interactions end-to-end, from bookings and dispatches to customer inquiries, reminders, surveys, and lead engagement, helping organizations answer every call and reach customers at the right moment.

name: K Line Europe
description: While deeptech solutions are revamping many facets of healthcare, dentistry has stayed immune to many of their economic and ecological advances. K Line Europe’s flagship product, ClearX, is the first dental aligner to leverage IoT. Its remote monitoring system allows patients to check their treatment process and modify the aligners’ fit without needing a new pair of aligners each time – or a time-consuming visit to the dentist’s office.

name: Cybernetex
description: Their aim is to enable companies to better identify, respond to, and avoid cybersecurity breaches. Cybernetex demonstrates the efficacy of their machine learning approach, and advance state-of-the art on the path towards increasingly general AI.

name: singa
description: Karaoke is the last analog bastion of the entertainment industry and Singa is the first one to give a damn about the market and bring it to the 21st century. With Singa you can stream karaoke anywhere, any device and at any time from mobile to desktops and smart devices. Singa gives you access to over 80,000 songs from classics to new hits. Whether you want to sing by yourself, throw a karaoke party, or are looking for professional karaoke software for your business, Singa has your back.

name: outshifter
description: Every eCommerce system manages its product data in a unique way. This gives an unprecedented advantage to sales channels with access to product data. As a result, large international marketplaces like Facebook, Amazon and Zalando dominate the space. Leaving behind a long tail of companies struggling to scale and monetize with eCommerce. Outshifter is leveling the playing field by allowing suppliers to share access to their product data with multiple third parties at the same time, in one universal format.

name: Metaktik
description: Metaktik is a Finnish deep-tech company founded by Tuukka Kuuramaa and Ville Lundén, building ultra-lightweight, high-performance metasurface antenna solutions for the aerospace, defense, security, and telecom sectors. Its technology delivers advanced radar and communication capabilities across land, sea, air, and space, combining precision, adaptability, and low-signature design in mission-critical environments.

name: Onio
description: As the Internet of Things expands, so does the challenge of powering billions of devices without adding to the world’s battery waste. ONiO tackles this with a breakthrough microcontroller that runs entirely on ambient energy, harvesting power from light, heat, radio waves, or motion. ONiO.zero integrates processing, connectivity, and power management on a single chip, enabling battery-free or ultra-low-power devices for applications in agriculture, logistics, retail, and smart buildings. No charging, just efficient, autonomous operation.

name: financekey
description: Manual workflows and fragmented systems continue to slow down finance teams in large organizations. FinanceKey has built an AI-driven treasury automation platform that connects banking, ERP, and treasury systems into one unified solution, giving enterprises real-time cash visibility, automated payments, and full control over financial operations. Founded by former Nokia treasury leaders Veikko Koski, Macer Skeels, Tiago Batista, and Rony Meyer, FinanceKey empowers finance teams to replace outdated processes with intelligent automation, enabling faster, smarter, and more strategic decision-making at scale.

name: revonte
description: The electronic bike market is growing rapidly, but to make it even more competitive the riding experience must be enhanced and simplified. Revonte’s techonology gives manufacturers more flexibility, provides better after-sale services, and improves the user experience. Their e-bike drive system comes with integrated automatic transmission, built-in connectivity, and full customization. The service also includes a mobile app and cloud services to provide a holistic user experience for e-bike riders.

name: Tracksight
description: Market data fragmentation poses a significant challenge in the global automotive industry. TrackSights has built an AI-driven intelligence platform that collects key automotive and vehicle-specific data to create a one-stop platform giving users a 360° view of both the global market and specific cars or fleets, enabling faster and smarter decision-making. Founded by Mark Lunding Pedersen, Magnus Wasteson and Anders Holm-Jensen, Tracksights helps car leasing companies, dealerships, financiers, and insurers make smarter, data-driven decisions with ease.

name: sera
description: Sera is fixing what AI broke in sales. Rather than blasting inboxes with generic, automated messages, Sera’s AI sales agent researches, qualifies, and personalizes every interaction. With Sera, sales teams cut hours of repetitive work while achieving qualification rates up to 5× higher than the industry standard. Founded in Estonia, Sera is trusted by companies like Bolt, Ready Player Me, and Montonio. Its strongest impact is seen in export-driven manufacturers, where Sera has helped secure international partnerships worth millions in new revenue, all while lowering the cost of scaling sales teams.

name: zevoy
description: Companies spend a vast amount of time and money on financial services. With Zevoy, they can simplify their expense management and focus on the business. Zevoy’s technology offers a smarter and faster all-in-one software. It combines Zevoy’s business card with a receipt scanning app and administration portal, and automates all company expenses in real-time – increasing employee satisfaction along the way. This team is now paving the way for Nordic fintech, and by the end of 2021, Zevoy will expand its operations to multiple European markets and become the leading expense management solution provider over time.

name: yaak
description: Driver coaching is a market that has seen very little innovation over the years. While ineffective driver training is costing €25B annually, a growing instructor shortage has driving schools buckling under increasing demands and narrowing profit margins. Yaak Technologies presents SafetyOS—the ultimate driving coaching platform that ties together 360 degree vision-based driver coaching, in-vehicle VR simulation training and consolidated safety scoring. Simulation lessons are cheaper and enable students to train good driving habits effectively, while allowing instructors to simply handle more students.

name: Volare
description: Insect proteins can significantly reduce the environmental load of animal feed, pet food and cosmetics industries. With the purest form of circularity, Volare radically reduces the environmental burden of the food chain. Volare uses food production side streams, such as non-edible parts of grains, to produce high-quality proteins and oils in order to replace other animal proteins, soy and palm oil. 100% new products, 0% new side streams.

name: Valpas
description: Valpas is the hygiene protocol that reassures travellers and keeps hotels clean from the most uncontrollable: bed bugs. Valpas ensures travellers stay and return home safe from these unwanted guests and solves the biggest unsolved hygiene problem in living spaces worldwide. Described as “an answered prayer to travellers everywhere”, Valpas has become an industry standard. Valpas’ smart bed legs capture the first few bed bugs before infestations, and the hotel staff is notified of the captured bed bugs by email. The room cleanliness can be monitored with the Valpas web app 24/7.

name: Spinnova
description: Spinnova is on a mission to create a more sustainable textile industry. One where cellulose-based materials are a cost-efficient, environmentally friendly and preferred option for brands. The current manufacturing processes rely mostly on non-renewable resources such as oil, fertilizers and dye, while consuming globally 93 billion cubic meters of water annually. That’s nearly the amount of water in the Dead Sea.

name: TOTEM
description: TOTEM is a modern concept of office stores including quality snacking and customizable food & convenience services designed for companies who value human interactions, co-workers’ well-being and respect for the environment. TOTEM believes your company shouldn’t have to be Google to be able to provide an amazing employee experience. Instead, this should be accessible for everyone at a lower cost and with convenient options.

name: Sidos
description: Sidos delivers professional-grade Wi-Fi tools that are powerful, precise, intuitive, and easy to use. The company’s mission is to help Wi-Fi professionals solve tough Wi-Fi challenges, eliminating guesswork and non-value-added tasks. Sidos takes pride in developing tools that are easy to use yet deliver precise and reliable results. With Sidos´s products, Wi-Fi professionals can quickly and accurately survey, troubleshoot, and optimize Wi-Fi networks, improving connectivity and performance for their clients.

name: twice
description: On its way to become a category-defining brand, Twice Commerce is uniquely positioned in the rapidly growing $250+ billion recommerce market. By offering a robust infrastructure for resales, rentals, and returns, Twice Commerce empowers emerging and existing brands to embrace the paradigm shift towards circular economies helping the world to decouple economic growth from material extraction. Our investment in Twice Commerce underscores our commitment to fostering innovative solutions that drive sustainable and profitable growth in the commerce sector.

name: Quanscient
description: Companies innovating in deep tech fields, from fusion energy and aerospace to electric motors and 5G technology, rely heavily on simulations to provide feedback for product development. However, existing solutions come with high costs and other inefficiencies resulting in long waits before bringing products to the market. As world’s first cloud-and-quantum-computing-powered multiphysics simulation technology provider, Quanscient is radically accelerating simulations and transforming R&D processes across multiple industries. Quanscient doesn’t only enable speedy and highly complex R&D – their better simulations also help to make products more energy efficient and sustainable.

name: Aisti
description: A sought-after feature of any indoor space is the acoustics—in other words how peaceful and quiet it can really be. And this makes acoustic tiles a key element of modern construction. However, the solutions widely used today are highly carbon intensive. To add to that the end products (made of insulating materials like glass wool or rock wool) are non-recyclable and can cause irritability. All too much of a price to pay for silence. Now Aisti is stepping in to change that with their novel acoustic tile—a natural, healthy and environmentally friendly solution for modern construction needs.

name: QDI Systems
description: QDI Systems from Groningen, the Netherlands, is the first initiative worldwide that is able to demonstrate the added value of quantum dots for X-ray examinations. The technology is based on ultra-modern nanomaterial: quantum dots. This material converts photons into electronic signals in a highly effective way. When quantum dots are used for X-ray examinations, they are able to create a higher image quality at lower radiation doses. The technology is expected to have a huge impact on procedures like mammogram screening and diagnostics.

name: ogoship

With their worldwide fulfillment network and smart local-like shipments, businesses can ship globally and sustainably. OGOship customers can store their goods in several warehouse locations, sell products in multiple online stores and use one inventory, and manage everything with one Order Management System.

name: Neuro event lab

Currently, 30% of diagnosed epilepsy cases are later disproved by new methods, and one-third of epilepsy patients continue to have seizures regardless of treatment. Neuro Event Labs has developed an AI-powered epilepsy diagnostic, which is based on video and audio recordings that can be collected from either the patient’s home or in hospital. Nelli™ is CE-marked and has been launched for regular clinical use at 20 leading European hospitals, and used in collaboration with hospitals in the US.

name: Membrane Finance

Fiat or government issued currencies not pegged to a commodity like gold are inherently incompatible with digital currencies. Today, stablecoins are the go-between for traditional finance and virtual currencies. While USD stablecoins are gaining a stronghold in this multi trillion market, EURO is trailing behind without an established equivalent. Membrane Finance is bridging this gap through EUROe which will also provide fast, inexpensive and regulatory-compliant access to DeFI markets.

In cloud gaming, a game is computed in internet-connected datacenters, and then the results are sent via video to a user’s screen. That enables gaming on various machines, be it a low-end laptop, a desktop gaming PC, a mobile device, or a console display such as a TV.

description: The Fepi는 브랜드 OEM 공장 잉여재고를 직접 소싱하여 판매하는 SEA 오프프라이스 (Off-price) 플랫폼입니다.

name: 스마투스코리아
description: 스마투스는 광센서를 이용한 정량화된 치아우식 진단 및 측정 의료기기 장비입니다.

name: 스캐터랩
description: 유저가 일주일에 10시간을 체류하는 AI 엔터테인먼트 서비스 "제타"를 만들고 있습니다.

name: 스크리나
description: 카라라는 버추얼 유튜버들의 노래 방송을 보조하는 프로그램입니다.

name: 스타일쉐어
description: 스타일쉐어는 10~20대 여성을 주 타깃으로 하는 국내 1위 패션·뷰티 커뮤니티 기반의 커머스 플랫폼입니다. 2021년 국내 최대 패션 플랫폼 무신사에 인수되었습니다.

name: 스텝하우
description: 스텝하우 팀은 사내 문서 탐색, 분석, 활용 등 문서 업무를 자동화하는 AI 솔루션 'Wissly'를 운영하고 있습니다.

name: 시소
description: 시소는 N잡러 기반의 스타트업 방식의 애자일한 아웃소싱 솔루션을 제공하고, 채용공고 데이터를 수집 분석해 AI 기반 커리어 탐색 서비스를 제공합니다.

name: 시프티
description: 시프티는 출퇴근 기록, 근무 일정, 휴가, 전자결재 등을 통합 제공하는 국내 선도적인 통합 인력관리 SaaS(서비스형 소프트웨어) 솔루션입니다. 2022년 비즈니스온에 인수된 후, 2024년 스카이레이크 에쿼티 파트너스가 인수하여 독립 경영 체제로 전환하며 성장세를 이어가고 있습니다.

name: 아르토에이아이
description: 산업 현장을 위한 온디바이스 음성 AI를 개발합니다.

name: 아슬론
description: 아슬론은 12-lead ECG 데이터로 관상동맥 협착을 조기 예측하여 심근경색을 예방하는 인공지능 솔루션 기업입니다.

name: 아이와트립
description: 아이와트립은 영유아 동반 가족을 위한 프리미엄 여행 및 체험 상품 플랫폼 '동키' 운영사입니다. 2022년 국내 대표 트래블테크 기업 마이리얼트립에 인수되었습니다.

name: 알로하팩토리
description: 알로하팩토리는 자체 솔루션(플라밍고)을 통한 라이트코어 캐주얼게임 개발/퍼블리싱/마케팅 서비스를 제공합니다.

name: 알파아시아
description: 워프코퍼레이션은 스포츠 IP 기반의 마케팅 상품을 개발합니다.

name: 애딧앤아크코퍼레이션
description: AI로 인스타그램 오가닉뷰 광고 시장을 개척하는 K-컬처 비즈니스 플랫폼

name: 앤트
description: 랩노트는 바이오, 나노, 화학 분야에 특화된 연구 데이터 통합 기록 및 관리 솔루션입니다.

name: 어글리랩
description: 어글리랩은 쓰레기 배출의 번거로움을 해결하는 문전수거 서비스 '오늘수거'를 운영하는 스타트업입니다.

name: 언커먼홈
description: 나르카는 헤어&바디케어의 Restore & Restyle 브랜드 입니다.

name: 업스테어스
description: 폰가비는 중고폰 견적 산정·비교 서비스를 제공하는 온라인 중고폰 거래 중개 플랫폼입니다.

name: 에스테이트클라우드
description: 우대빵은 아파트 매물보유 1위 중개기업으로 전통적인 중개서비스에 기술을 더해 고객들에게 더 나은 중개서비스 경험을 제공합니다.

name: 에이든랩
description: 인코드8은 AI 기반 글로벌 마케팅&이커머스 솔루션입니다.

name: 에이아이닷엠
description: 셀롸이트는 상세페이지 상품 설명을 자동 생성하는 서비스입니다.

name: 에임인텔리전스
description: 생성형 AI 보안 진단 및 취약점 자동 탐지/차단 솔루션

name: 에프랩앤컴퍼니
description: 에프랩은 상위 1% 개발자들의 멘토링으로 계층 이동의 사다리를 만듭니다.

name: 엔츠
description: 엔스코프는 기업을 위한 탄소중립 관리 플랫폼입니다.

name: 엠젯패밀리
description: 엠젯패밀리는 웹툰, 웹소설 및 굿즈를 제작 및 유통하는 글로벌 콘텐츠 기업입니다.

name: 예스비
description: K 브랜드와 전세계 바이어를 연결하는 플랫폼 서비스로, 효율적인 공급망 관리를 지원합니다.

name: 오내피플
description: 캐치시큐는 AI 및 SaaS 기반 개인정보보호 규제 자동화 준수 서비스입니다.

name: 오앤비스페이스
description: 오앤비스페이스는 독자적인 위성 기술과 고정밀 우주 데이터를 바탕으로 뉴스페이스 시대를 선도하는 딥테크 우주 스타트업입니다.

name: 오픈에셋
description: 오픈에셋은 금융기관들의 자산을 혁신적인 토큰으로 전환시키는 블록체인 기반 솔루션을 제공합니다.

name: 옴니어스
description: 옴니커머스는 태깅, 추천, 개인화, 상품 관리 및 분석 등 고객의 쇼핑 경험을 향상시키는 이커머스 필수 AI 솔루션을 제공합니다.

name: 옵트에이아이
description: 옵트에이아이는 엣지 AI 도입을 위한 최적화 기술을 제공합니다.

name: 와이즈모바일
description: 파킹박은 주차장 정보를 제공하고 제휴된 주차장의 주차권을 할인 판매하는 서비스입니다.

name: 와이피랩스
description: 커넥팅은 음성 커뮤니케이션을 기반으로 사람과 사람이 연결되는 방식을 혁신하는 서비스입니다.

name: 우트
description: 타입스는 만나고 싶은 사람들과 원할 때 모일 수 있는 모바일 솔루션 앱입니다.

name: 운칠기삼
description: 포스텔러는 사주, 별자리, 타로 등 동서양의 오래된 운세 콘텐츠를 시대적 배경과 최신 스마트 기기 환경에 맞춰 새롭게 풀이해주는 콘텐츠 서비스입니다.

name: 원데이원송
description: 원데이원송은 모바일 음악 추천 서비스입니다.

name: 웨딩북
description: 웨딩북은 IT를 기반으로 결혼 시장을 혁신하고 있는 스타트업으로 웨딩북, 웨딩북비즈, 웨딩북청담, 웨딩북사이공을 서비스합니다.

name: 이숲컴퍼니
description: 이숲컴퍼니는 온라인스토어 평가의 신뢰도를 높여 최적화된 파이낸싱과 경영지원을 제공합니다.

name: 이코니크
description: 이코니크는 데이터와 기술을 바탕으로 F&B 시장을 혁신하는 푸드테크 기업입니다.

name: 인디드랩
description: 다년간 축적한 아파트 계획/분석/평가 기술을 근간으로 데이터 기반 아파트 가치 평가 서비스, '더스택'을 운영하고 있습니다.

name: 인포그린
description: 맘가이드는 방대한 국내외 유해성분 데이터를 기반으로 유아용품 유해성분 정보를 제공하는 안심 제품 큐레이션 앱입니다.

name: 임플로이랩스
description: 잡브레인은 검증 기반의 보상형 채용 플랫폼입니다.

name: 작당모의
description: 잼페이스는 뷰티에 특화된 인공지능과 증강현실 기술로 퍼스널 컬러와 피부 타입 등 뷰티 타입을 진단하고, 각 타입에 맞는 화장품을 추천해주는 뷰티 플랫폼입니다.

name: 잘라컴퍼니
description: 잘라는 인터넷 방송 영상 편집에 특화된 AI 기반 컷 편집점 추천 프로그램입니다.

name: 제로원리퍼블릭
description: 스코디는 기업용 소프트웨어 툴 (SaaS) 구독 관리 서비스입니다.

name: 제이오에프엔비
description: 제이오에프엔비는 브랜드 '조우'로 한우기반 HMR 식품제조 및 외식사업을 운영합니다.

name: 지니파이
description: 지피터스는 커뮤니티 기반의 AI 교육 프로그램을 운영하며, 강사 없이 학습하는 AI 시대의 학습 플랫폼을 만듭니다.

name: 짐워크
description: 짐워크는 개인 맞춤형 운동 프로그램과 데이터 분석으로 건강한 성장을 지원하는 피트니스 앱입니다.

name: 짜이서울
description: 짜이서울은 방한 중국인 관광객을 타겟으로 하는 한국 여행 전문 온·오프라인 플랫폼으로 2015년 NICE 그룹으로부터 인수되었습니다.

name: 짧은대본
description: 짧은대본은 유튜브를 중심으로 뉴미디어 영상콘텐츠를 제작합니다.

name: 차트메트릭
description: 차트메트릭은 음악 산업에서 사용되는 데이터 분석 플랫폼입니다.

name: 카드몬스터
description: 카드몬은 AI로 브랜드와 아이디어를 게임으로 구현하는 게임 테크 기업입니다.

name: 카사네트워크
description: 카사는 싱가포르에서 기관투자자, 패밀리오피스 그리고 자산가를 대상으로 전세계 다양한 부동산 투자건들을 소개합니다.

name: 컨포트랩
description: 컨포트랩은 제조 AX 구축을 표준화한 AI OS로 공장의 설비·품질·생산 운영을 지능화하는 기업입니다.

name: 케이존
description: REMEX는 기업들이 악성재고로 겪는 경제적 손실 문제를 재판매를 통해 해결해드리는 플랫폼입니다.

name: 코어사이트
description: 씽크코어는 게임에서 발생하는 모든 데이터를 수집, 저장, 분석, 시각화해 게임개발사 및 퍼블리셔에게 실시간으로 정보를 제공하는 SaaS 서비스입니다.

name: 쿼키
description: ConstrucKit은 건설 프로젝트 팀을 위한 문서 기반 커뮤니케이션 시스템입니다.

name: 쿼타랩
description: 쿼타북은 스타트업 및 투자자가 증권 및 경영 관련 제반 사항을 편리하게 관리할 수 있도록 돕는 증권 관리 플랫폼입니다.

name: 큐스템
description: 큐스템은 hiPSC로부터 분화시킨 모유두세포를 활용하여 탈모개선 전문기업을 지향하고 있습니다.

name: 키뮤
description: 키뮤스튜디오는 발달장애인 디자이너의 특별한 디자인이 담긴 콘텐츠 중심의 B2C 브랜드입니다.

name: 탠덤스튜디오
description: 화장품, 의류, 패션잡화, 라이프스타일 등 K-뷰티 멀티브랜드 하우스

name: 테르밋
description: 테르밋은 온라인 판매에 필요한 마케팅 콘텐츠 제작을 AI로 자동화하는 서비스, 크리에이지를 운영합니다.

name: 테이밍랩
description: 럭셔리 워치 버티컬 커머스 왓타임을 운영 중인 스타트업입니다.

name: 테이스트샵/언리얼모닝
description: 그림의빵은 혈당이 오르지 않는 대체 밀가루를 사용한 베이커리입니다.

name: 텐핑
description: 텐핑은 광고주와 1인 퍼포먼스 마케터들을 연결하는 마케팅 플랫폼입니다.

name: 토글랩스
description: 토글은 온라인 판매자들을 대상으로 쇼핑몰 통합관리 솔루션과 소싱 대행 서비스를 제공합니다.

name: 토끼와두꺼비
description: 똑비는 시니어를 위한 개인비서 서비스입니다.

name: 토이스미스
description: 토이스미스는 IoT 센서를 통해 다양한 데이터를 수집하고, 빅데이터를 기반으로 다양한 분석을 제공하는 스마트시티 솔루션입니다.

name: 투이지
description: AI 캐릭터 숏폼 생성 서비스 "부캐공장"을 운영합니다. 단 한 장의 사진으로 무한한 캐릭터 숏폼 콘텐츠를 경험하세요.

name: 튜링
description: AI로 수학·과학 문제 해결을 혁신하는 글로벌 STEM AI 에이전트 기업

name: 튜터링
description: 튜터링은 전 세계 전문 튜터와 학생을 실시간으로 연결하는 온디맨드(On-Demand) 모바일 외국어 학습 플랫폼입니다. 2018년 매칭마켓 컴퍼니 빌더 마켓디자이너스와 합병하여 사업을 확장했습니다.

name: 트러스트랩스
description: 썰즈는 디지털의료를 활용한 남성 메디컬 브랜드입니다.

name: 티냅스
description: PoC에 멈춘 AI를 실제 비즈니스로 이끄는 AI 런타임 신뢰 인프라

name: 팀모노리스
description: 전국 1,200개교 이상이 도입한 AI 기반 통합 교육 플랫폼 '코들'

name: 팁코퍼레이션
description: TIPP은 B2B 리더십 코칭 플랫폼으로, 사내 리더들에게 개인화된 리더십 코칭을 제공하여 리더십 성장과 업무 생산성 향상을 지원합니다.

name: 패러닷
description: 캐럿은 콘텐츠 특화 AI 에이전트입니다. 전문가에게 업무를 맡기는 것처럼, AI에게 고품질 콘텐츠 제작을 요청할 수 있습니다.

name: 퍼플에이아이

name: Abwab.ai
description: Abwab supports banks, NBFIs, fintechs, funds, and platforms originate, decide, and grow their MSME book with AI across the full lending lifecycle

name: Altibbi
description: Altibbi is the leading digital health platform in the Arab world, providing telemedicine consultations, and medical content. It connects patients with certified doctors and offers 24/7 remote healthcare services. The platform aims to improve healthcare accessibility across MENA.. The digital health platform has 192M+ users with millions of consultations and recommendations provided annually.

name: Anghami
description: Anghami is the leading music and audio streaming platform in the MENA region, offering Arabic and international content across music, podcasts, and entertainment. It operates a freemium model with premium subscriptions and strategic partnerships with telcos. The company is publicly listed on NASDAQ following its SPAC merger. The MENA music platform has 120M+ users, 3.5M+ subscribers, and ~$48M H1 revenue across 16 markets.

name: Basma
description: Basma is a healthtech company specializing in digital orthodontics, offering at-home teeth straightening solutions supported by remote monitoring. It combines telehealth with customized treatment plans. Basma aims to make orthodontic care more accessible and affordable.

name: Bevy (Previously Eventtus)
description: Bevy is a community management platform that enables brands to build, manage, and scale global communities through events and engagement tools. It evolved from Eventtus into a broader SaaS platform supporting virtual, hybrid, and in-person events. Bevy serves enterprises looking to drive customer engagement.

name: Bykea
description: Bykea is a ride-hailing and logistics platform in Pakistan offering bike rides, deliveries, and payments services. It leverages a large network of riders to provide affordable mobility and last-mile delivery. The platform targets mass-market urban users. The Super app has 5M users and 1.7M monthly active users in Pakistan.

name: Clinicy
description: Clinicy is a healthcare SaaS platform that provides clinics and medical practices with digital tools for patient management, scheduling, and electronic medical records. It streamlines clinic operations and improves patient experience. The platform targets small to mid-sized healthcare providers. Healthcare SaaS driving 2M SAR Annual Revenue Recovered (532,800 USD) for clinics.

name: Cognitev (previously MENA Commerce)
description: Cognitev is an AI-powered advertising technology company that enables automated media buying and campaign optimization. It leverages machine learning to improve ad performance across digital channels. The company operates globally with a focus on performance marketing with 150+ professionals and 6 innovation initiatives.

name: Cookpad (previously Shahiya)
description: Cookpad is a global recipe-sharing platform that enables users to discover and share home-cooked meals. Shahiya was its leading Arabic platform prior to acquisition. The platform monetizes through subscriptions and community-driven content.

name: Designer 24
description: Designer-24 is a luxury fashion rental platform in the Middle East (UAE, Lebanon, and Jordan) that makes high-end designer clothing accessible to women. It offers curated, on-trend looks for various occasions while promoting sustainability and women empowerment by reducing the need for fast fashion purchases.

name: Dixio
description: Dixio is a fintech infrastructure company providing API-based connectivity between financial institutions, corporates, and payment systems. Its platform enables secure, standardized messaging and integration across banking networks. Dixio focuses on simplifying financial data exchange and interoperability. Cross-border payments infrastructure serving 200+ clients across 60+ countries.

name: Eat
description: Eat is a restaurant technology platform providing POS systems, reservations, and customer management solutions for the hospitality industry. It helps restaurants digitize operations and improve customer engagement. Eat covers 90+ countries, 5K+ restaurants, and 80+ hotel groups.

name: Erad
description: Erad is a fintech that specializes in providing financial solutions for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in KSA and UAE

name: Fadel
description: Fadel is a rights and royalty management software provider for media, publishing, and entertainment industries. Its platform enables companies to manage intellectual property rights, contracts, and revenue distribution. Fadel serves global enterprise clients reducing their processing time by 50% and asset clearance time by 70%.

name: FlapKap
description: FlapKap is a fintech platform providing revenue-based financing solutions to e-commerce and digital businesses. It enables merchants to access non-dilutive capital based on their sales performance. The platform uses data integrations to underwrite and deploy funding quickly.

name: Fresha
description: Fresha is a global SaaS marketplace for beauty and wellness businesses, offering booking, payments, and customer management tools. It operates a commission-free model for merchants while monetizing through payments and add-ons. Fresha serves millions of users across salons and spas worldwide. Global beauty & wellness platform powering 130K+ businesses and 1B+ bookings across 120+ countries.

name: Fundbot
description: Fundbot is a supply chain financing platform that provides SMEs with working capital by financing invoices and purchase orders. It leverages alternative data and fintech infrastructure to improve credit access. The platform connects businesses, lenders, and financial institutions.

name: Hala
description: Hala is an SME-focused fintech providing digital payment solutions, including POS systems, payment acceptance, and business management tools—enabling small merchants to seamlessly accept and manage transactions. The SME-focused fintech processes $6B+ in transactions with 100K users and is licensed by SAMA.

name: HyperPay
description: HyperPay is a payment gateway platform in MENA enabling businesses to accept online payments securely. It supports multiple payment methods and provides fraud protection and analytics tools. The company serves e-commerce and enterprise clients processing 2,400+ TPS across 10K+ merchants in 9 countries.

name: Invygo
description: Invygo is a car subscription platform offering flexible, hassle-free vehicle access without long-term commitments. Users can subscribe to cars through a fully digital process. The platform targets urban consumers seeking mobility flexibility. The car subscription platform has 20K+ active users across 15+ cities in UAE & KSA.

name: KamelPay
description: KamelPay is a digital payments platform enabling secure online transactions and financial services for consumers and merchants. It offers wallet solutions, payment processing, and financial access tools. The platform focuses on expanding digital payment adoption in underserved markets with 210K+ cards in circulation.

name: Keyper
description: Keyper is a property management platform that enables landlords to manage rentals, tenants, and payments digitally. It offers tools for leasing, maintenance, and financial tracking. Keyper aims to simplify real estate asset management by enabling paying rent in monthly instalments. Property management platform handling 2,200+ properties worth AED 12.8B and AED 71M in annual rent.

name: Lamsa
description: Lamsa is a digital education platform offering interactive Arabic content for children, including games, stories, and learning activities. It focuses on early childhood development through engaging digital experiences.

name: IMV Technologies

name: INGENYX

name: ISI Markets
description: ISI Markets is the leading provider of macroeconomic data, industry, company and sovereign intelligence.

name: ITRS Group
description: ITRS Group is a leading global provider of IT operations monitoring and analytics software for the “always on” enterprise, used by >3,000 clients globally to manage their operations and ensure operational resilience.

name: Janes
description: A leading provider of open source intelligence, providing timely information and data for industries including aerospace, defence, and security. Montagu completed the acquisition of Janes from IHS Markit in December 2019.

name: Lighteum Medical
description: Lighteum Medical develops and manufactures critical and complex miniature components for minimally invasive medical devices used in high-growth clinical specialties. It focuses on complex and high-precision components made from Platinum Group Metals and Nitinol, with decades of expertise in the metallurgy, micromachining, and advanced Nitinol processing.

name: Lloyd’s List Intelligence
description: Provider of market-leading products offering reliable, high-quality maritime data and actionable analytics, with mission-critical applications across compliance, risk management and operations.

name: Maincare
description: Provider of software for French public hospitals and state-run health authorities. Maincare addresses the critical software needs of health organisations through an integrated suite of products spanning electronic patient records, population health solutions, and back-office tools.

name: Marlow Foods
description: A manufacturer of an extensive range of branded chilled and frozen ingredients and meals from its manufacturing base in north Yorkshire. Quorn was the UK’s number one brand in the fast-growing healthy meat alternative food segment with an established and successful presence in a number of European territories. Montagu led the buyout of Marlow Foods, the owner of Quorn-branded food products, in the first half of 2003 from AstraZeneca. Following our acquisition of the business, Marlow Foods performed strongly in its core European territories and grew rapidly in the US from a standing start in 2002. In June 2005 we sold Marlow Foods to Premier Foods Plc.

name: Miraclon
description: One of the world’s leading providers of imaging technologies for the graphics customisation of printed packaging materials. Montagu completed the acquisition of Kodak’s Flexographic Packaging Division in April 2019. Shortly after the transaction closed, the business was renamed “Miraclon”. Miraclon’s flagship flexographic plate imaging system, FLEXCEL NX, has received industry-wide acclaim for its leading image resolution quality, since debuting on the market in 2008. Flexography is the most common form of packaging printing and can apply images on almost any substrate, with a speciality in flexible packaging.

name: Multifonds
description: Multifonds, founded in 1995 in Luxembourg, is a global provider of proprietary investment accounting and transfer agency software used to perform a range of back- and middle-office fund services tasks. The platform supports over 40,000 funds and more than $10 trillion in assets across 35+ jurisdictions.

name: Nemera
description: A proven, rapidly growing producer of complex drug delivery systems. Nemera designs and manufactures a full range of drug delivery systems including asthma inhalers, insulin pens, auto-injectors and nasal pumps. The Nemera Group originally comprised two businesses at acquisition in May 2014: a healthcare devices business (Nemera) as well as a prescription retail containers and closures business (Centor, which was sold in 2015), both carved-out of Rexam plc. In January 2019, we reinvested in Nemera alongside another investor to support the next phase of Nemera’s growth.

name: OASIS Group
description: A European provider of records and information management services across the UK, Ireland, the Netherlands, Poland and Belgium. OASIS’s services allow its customers to manage their records holistically and cost-effectively across the entire document lifecycle and help ensure regulatory compliance.

name: Risdon Pharma
description: A leading European manufacturer of primary plastic packaging for the pharmaceutical industry. Risdon Pharma was the European leader in blow moulded containers such as eye droppers and nasal sprays, and a major player in the fast-growing segment of drug delivery systems, such as metered dosage anti-asthma inhalers. In March 2002, Montagu acquired Risdon Pharma from Crown Cork and Seal Inc. (“Crown”) for €97 million. name: Sebia
description: A global leader in the diagnostics of serum protein with a superior technology in electrophoresis. Sebia is a research-driven company covering several pathologies including multiple myeloma, diabetes (HbA1c) and haemoglobin deficiencies. Montagu originally acquired the business in 2006 and invested for a second time in 2014.

name: Servelec
description: A provider of healthcare and case management software to NHS trusts and local authorities. Servelec has a focus in mental health, community care and interoperability and Montagu acquired it in January 2018 in a take-private transaction.

name: Stabilus
description: A market-leading manufacturer of gas springs, hydraulic vibration dampers, continuously adjustable doorstays and automatic opening and closing systems for doors, trunk lids and tailgates. Stabilus’s diversified customer base with long standing and close customer relationships, its unrivalled market position and strong management team made it an ideal investment for Montagu. In August 2004 Montagu led the Management Buyout of Stabilus, at that time a subsidiary of Demag Sarl a conglomerate owned by KKR and Siemens. In May 2008 Stabilus was sold to Paine & Partners, LLC, US-based private equity firm.

name: Steam Packet Company
description: Montagu led the Management Buyout in July 2003 from Sea Containers. The Steam Packet Company had a dominant position in the transportation of passengers and freight to the Isle of Man from ports in the UK underpinned by a long-standing user agreement with the Isle of Man government. The Steam Packet represented a very high quality, secure and cash generative business growing in line with a robust Manx economy. These features made it ideal for a leveraged buyout and as such our success in buying this business was at the end of a fiercely fought private equity auction. In October 2005 Montagu sold the Isle of Man Steam Packet Company to Macquarie Bank.

name: Survitec
description: The world’s leading survival technology company focused on serving the marine, military, aerospace and homeland security markets. In August 2004, Montagu led the Management Buyout of The Survitec Group, a division of Air-Sea Survival Equipment Limited, which was controlled by the Alchemy Investment Plan. We backed the management team with follow on capital to both make further acquisitions and to fund the move of some of its manufacturing into low cost territories. In February 2010, Survitec was sold to Warburg Pincus.

name: The University of Law
description: The leading provider of professional legal education and training in England and Wales. The University of Law focused principally on the provision of post-graduate legal training through the Legal Practice Course (LPC) and the Graduate Diploma in Law (GDL). The business was founded in 1962 and was originally set up as a not-for-profit Royal Charter charitable corporation. It was known as the College of Law until 2012 but it was awarded University status following our investment.

name: Ultra Electronics
description: Ultra Electronics is a group of businesses that manage a portfolio of specialist capabilities, generating highly differentiated solutions and products in the defence & aerospace, security & cyber, transport and energy markets by applying electronic and software technologies in demanding and critical environments to meet customer needs. Montagu backed the management buy-out of seven businesses of the Dowty Electronics Systems Division of Dowty Group in 1993 and was made public on the London Stock Exchange in 1996.

name: Universal Investment
description: Universal Investment is a European third-party management company (“ManCo”) and fund administration service provider, serving institutional investors and asset managers. Founded in 1968 as a joint venture of German private banks, it was owned by Berenberg and Bankhaus Lampe before Montagu acquired it in a carve-out in January 2017.

name: VetXX
description: Marketer of pharmaceutical products for skin, eye and ear diseases, and producer of pet diet food (through the brand SPECIFIC) and pet care products for companion animals. VetXX’s animal health products were distributed exclusively through veterinary surgeries in more than 35 countries. In March 2005, Montagu led and arranged the Management Buyout of Leo Animal Health (subsequently renamed VetXX) from its shareholder, the privately owned Danish pharmaceutical company Leo Pharma. In December 2007 VetXX was sold to Dechra Pharmaceuticals.

name: Visma
description: A provider of business management software in Northern Europe. Visma provides mission-critical financial, accounting, payroll and HR software primarily to SMEs and public sector organisations. Montagu was involved with Visma from its first minority investment in 2010, reinvestment in 2014 and again in 2017.

name: Volution
description: A leading supplier of ventilation products that, at the time of our investment, included Vent-Axia (ventilation), Kopex and Adaptaflex (ducting and fittings for electrical cables). In December 2002 Montagu led the Management Buyout of Smiths Group plc’s building products division, which was renamed Volution Holdings Limited. At the time of our approach, Smiths was considering separate disposals of its air movement and cable management divisions. We saw that both divisions were under common management and serving common customers and we approached Smiths Group with an offer for both divisions. This approach simplified the disposal for the vendor and had the support of management who had plans for both product groups. In May 2003 Volution disposed of Airstream, its washroom rentals division and in August 2006 Volution was sold to ABN AMRO Capital, the private equity arm of ABN AMRO.

name: Waystone Group
